presentation.explanation: A known 0.3 Hz sinusoid is added to the reference. Both the corrupted signal and the clean reference pass through the same second-order Butterworth high-pass filter, forward and backward. The clean-input branch exposes distortion caused by filtering itself.
presentation.limitation: Offline filtering uses future samples. These errors describe this synthetic waveform, not clinical acceptability or an optimal ECG cutoff.
presentation.question: How does the high-pass filter change the clean reference?
presentation.summary: A high-pass filter reduces slow drift. The same filter also changes parts of the original waveform.
presentation.title: Baseline-wander filtering
